title: Open a snapped-shut game case, press its hub to free the disc, then stand the disc up and slide it into a console slot
instruction: Open the game case, take the disc out and put it into the console.
context: Loading a game or film disc is an everyday task in homes with consoles and players, and it starts with a shut case. A game case snaps shut: pulling the cover's lip alone lifts the whole light case, so one hand holds the tray half down while the other opens the cover. Inside, the hub's spring teeth hold the disc: it comes off only while the hub's centre button is pressed, and lifting it otherwise lifts the case (and can crack a real disc), so one hand presses while the other lifts. The disc is wider than the gripper opens and 1.2 mm thick, so it is held by its edge and turned upright on the way, and a 5 mm slot leaves under 2 mm either side. No disc, game-case or console task is on the board.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A is given first, layout B in brackets. Console: a black games console with white side panels (10.4 cm wide, 26 cm deep, 30 cm tall), standing upright, fixed, its front face at x 47 facing the arms, centred at y 6. Its slot-loading drive's slot is vertical in the front face: 5 mm wide and 13.2 cm tall, its middle 10 cm above the table, behind a flared mouth 12 mm wide narrowing to 5 mm over 8 mm; the drive bay behind it is 13.5 cm deep. Storage box: a brown box 8.5 cm tall, 28 cm long (along x) and 18 cm wide, fixed, under the case and long enough for the opened cover to lie on. Game case: a plastic game case, 13.5 x 17.1 x 1.5 cm shut, 70 g, lying shut on the box with its cover up (dark blue, with an orange printed sleeve), its spine along the far long edge and its opening edge toward the arms, overhanging the box by 2.75 cm; the hub's axis (the case's middle) at x 43, y 21 [B: x 42, y 22]. The spine (1.5 cm) turns on the tray's far edge and the cover on the spine's top edge, a quarter turn each, so the opened cover lies flat on the box beyond the case. A catch at the opening edge holds the case shut: it lets go when the cover's lip is pulled up with 1.2 N (3.7 mm of lift). Lifting that edge of the whole shut case takes 0.42 N. The tray half (blue) has a thumb cut-out 44 mm wide and 32 mm deep in the middle of its opening edge; the cover's lip stands 4 mm proud over it. The cover has a finger recess in its left edge, 32 mm long and 30 mm deep, starting 22 mm from the opening edge, through which a ledge on the tray's rim shows (20 x 25 mm, its top 6 mm above the box). The hub: a seat ring 34 mm across, a post through the disc's hole, three spring teeth over the hole's edge, and a centre button 12 mm across that stands 7 mm proud and presses 2.5 mm (600 N/m); the teeth draw in while it is pressed 1.5 mm or more. Disc: a 120 mm disc, 1.2 mm thick, 15 mm hole, 16 g, blue label up, on the hub inside the shut case. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video and a ruler. 0 for the whole trial if at any time the disc touches the table outside the console (dropped). Otherwise 1.0 once the drive has taken the disc: it went in upright (within 10 degrees of square to the slot), centred (within 2.5 mm across the slot and 12 mm up or down) and 7 cm deep, and the drive drew it in. 0.75 if the disc stood in the slot at least 2 cm deep: its leading edge 2 cm or more behind the console's front face while it was upright and square to the slot (within 15 degrees) and all of it behind the face was inside the slot's opening, between its sides and its top and bottom ends (a disc held over the console, beside the slot or lying flat in its case does not count). 0.5 if it came off the hub (its centre 1 cm or more from its place on the hub). 0.25 if the case was opened where it lies (its cover swung upright, 90 degrees from shut, or further, while its tray half lay flat on the box). Else 0.
reset_notes: Eject the disc, put it back on the case's hub label up and press it home, shut the case until its catch snaps, and lay it on its box cover up, with the thumb cut-out toward the arms. Use a scratched spare disc for trials.
fidelity: Disc and case are rigid, real size. The catch is a spring at the cover's hinge that the task file lets go for good once the lip has been lifted 3.7 mm (1.2 N); the two living hinges are free quarter-turn joints. The hub's teeth are blocks the task file draws in while the sprung button is pressed. The drive is not modelled mechanically: once the disc is 7 cm in, upright and centred, the task file draws it in and holds it. The console and box are fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms stayed near their bases; the case was never touched and stayed shut); demo: 1.0 (case opened at step 360, disc 2 cm into the slot at step 835, drawn into the console at step 875)
